Reduce approach increments below the joint-continuity limit; continue left basket interception.

Replan from step 23 with slower right-arm forward motion and finish downward orientation above the basket side.
Track basket conveyor drift and cautiously close right gripper on the near right rim; retention still unverified.
Test basket rim retention by lifting 10 cm with right gripper closed, checking visual motion rather than gripper command.

Close around the right basket wall at rim depth while matching conveyor drift, then begin a small visual retention test.
Lift the right-held basket 9 cm and draw it inward while left arm prepares on its own side; verify basket follows the gripper.

Hold lifted basket centrally with the right arm; move left toward incoming conveyor items, seeking the board's gold clipper-shaped target rather than the blue bottle or white tool.
Keep basket suspended and withdraw left gripper from the white peeler, which does not match the gold image; improve head visibility of subsequent items.
Keep the lifted basket fixed and clear the conveyor viewing lane with the left arm while the image-matching item approaches.
The beige/gold incoming object matches the board silhouette and dark band. Begin left-arm interception while right keeps the basket lifted.
Approach above the beige target with open left fingers, allowing for continued belt motion. Basket remains suspended and right gripper stays closed.
After continuity interruption, use smaller forward increments and lower toward the target's midsection; estimated target is farther forward and left than the current fingers.
Lower first with only small forward motion to regain configuration margin; target continues moving toward the left gripper's interception area.
Match target conveyor motion, advance fingers to its beige midsection, and close for a grasp; retain the already lifted basket with right arm.
Forward reach hit IK limits before closure. Pitch the left fingers modestly forward while following the target, then close, keeping the arm configuration continuous.
Use smaller tilt and translation after zero-step rejection, keeping fingers open until aligned with the target.
Bring the slightly forward-tilted left fingers around the beige target while matching belt motion, then close for a visual lift test.
Wrist RGB confirms the board-matching beige doll at the closed fingers. Lift and retract gradually to test retention while maintaining the raised basket.
The doll remained on the belt after the lift test. Reopen and correct forward/depth alignment for a second grasp of its central body.
Wrist view places the doll's body ahead of the fingertips. Advance and deepen slightly while tracking, then close around the torso rather than the boots.
The doll torso is now visibly between the fingers. Keep closed and lift/retract in small continuous increments, checking that it follows.
Doll follows the left fingers during lift. Raise it further and retract before moving over the suspended basket, keeping both grasps closed.
Raise the retained doll above basket-rim height while drawing both objects slightly toward the robot for comfortable, uncrossed placement.
Carry the doll laterally over the basket opening with rim clearance, leaving the left EE on its own side and the right basket grip stationary.
Doll shifted sideways across the left basket rim rather than settling inside. Reopen and reposition around its torso for a controlled inward transfer; keep basket lifted.
Test the new doll grasp with a small lift and inward shift before release; the doll still spans the rim and retention is uncertain.
The doll slipped outside the basket. Move the open left gripper clear of the rim and down toward it for recovery, without releasing the suspended basket.
Retry recovery retreat at less than half the pose increment after the zero-step continuity rejection.
Recover the doll from the belt beside the basket; shift the still-lifted basket right to clear the left recovery approach.
Track the fallen sideways doll and rotate the open left jaws toward a cross-torso grasp, descending gradually while basket stays clear and elevated.
Finish aligning jaws across the sideways doll torso and close at belt level. Give basket another small rightward clearance while retaining its grip.
Lift-test the cross-torso grasp away from the basket wall, retaining both grips and checking the doll follows before another placement attempt.
Correct the rotated gripper's sideways fingertip offset: make it vertical and descend around the doll torso, while separating the basket to reduce interference.
Separate the basket farther right to remove contact interference, and test the closed left grasp by lifting and retracting on its own side.
Doll is now entering the right workspace. Bring the suspended basket centrally for a left-arm handoff, freeing the right arm to recover the doll without crossing arms.
Align left jaws across the basket's left wall and close as the right brings that wall into reach; do not release the right grip yet.
Test the basket handoff by keeping left closed and releasing right, then separating slowly. Verify basket follows left before right approaches the target.
Separate the basket toward the left and approach the doll with the freed right gripper. Basket retention after the handoff remains visually uncertain.
Handoff failed: basket is on belt. Reacquire its left rim at the new orientation while right moves forward toward the doll, keeping arms separated.
Right wrist sees doll ahead of the fingers; move forward and align jaws across its torso. Left follows the shifted basket rim for reacquisition.
Basket is caught against the right fingers and blocks the doll. Secure and retreat slowly to separate it from the target, with left arm clear.
Bring the caught basket centrally and lower toward a stable pose, undoing right wrist yaw; position left near the accessible rim without crossing.
Move the snagged basket away from the front edge and toward center, retaining arm separation. Left stays open for an accessible negative-x rim grasp.
Keep right fixed after the continuity interruption. Approach the basket's near-left wall with a modest inward fingertip tilt and close left for another controlled handoff.
Settle the left basket-wall closure, then release and withdraw right while left lifts and moves left. Check retention before proceeding to the doll.
Disengage the open right gripper toward the target side while left reaches the near basket wall more deeply; handoff retention is not established.
Prioritize the target before it exits the right workspace. Approach its torso with right while left clears; the basket can be filled and lifted again afterward.
Retry the unexecuted approach with reduced yaw and translation increments to satisfy wrist-joint continuity.
Continue rightward torso interception and descend while completing cross-body jaw alignment; close only after the approach, with left safely clear.
Replan smaller after the continuity stop: follow the doll rightward and lower around its torso, then close with limited forward reach.
Use a modest forward fingertip tilt rather than extending the arm farther forward; lower slightly, track slowly, and close around the doll.
The doll is aligned nearer the boots than torso. Reopen and shift along its body while retracting slightly for reach margin, then close for a final recovery grasp.
Lift and retract the closed right grasp to verify doll retention and regain reach margin; if retained, place into the basket before lifting basket again.
Doll remained on the belt. Reopen and approach its nearer end at a deeper grasp height, keeping the left arm clear and respecting the right reach guard.
After the continuity stop, use small wrist tilt and descent to reach the doll with the fingertips rather than extending the arm farther.
The doll is still below the fingertip contact area. Deepen and angle the right fingers farther along its nearer end with minimal arm translation, then close and settle.
Settle the closure and test retention with a small lift and inward retreat, rather than extending farther toward the conveyor edge.
Attempt a near-end grasp using outward fingertip inclination and a lower approach, without commanding full arm extension; retention remains unverified.
Allow the right closure to settle fully, then gently lift and retract to determine whether the doll is actually retained.
Wrist RGB shows the doll outside the closed fingers. Correct laterally toward the torso and lower the inclined fingertips for another grasp, with small continuous increments.
Make only a small open-finger correction toward the visible doll; do not assume retention, and avoid a large reach near the workspace boundary.
Tracking error increased near the conveyor edge and the doll remains outside the jaws. Back away upward and inward to preserve reach and contact safety.
Target remains on the belt beyond the safe grasp area. Retract both empty grippers within their own workspaces and monitor rather than overextend.
Continue controlled right-arm retreat with open fingers; target and basket are not retained and remain beyond the central working area.
Finish retracting the empty right gripper to a comfortable reach while monitoring the conveyor; no placement success is visible.
Basket contact caused a large tracking residual. Replan from the observed pose and withdraw right upward/backward in small increments with fingers open.
The retreat was rejected before execution. Hold the latest observed poses with open fingers to reestablish continuous tracking and let contact settle.
Tracking has settled. Withdraw the open right gripper gently upward and backward to clear the basket contact while keeping the left arm stationary.
Hold the latest observed poses with open grippers while residual contact settles. The target is not retained or placed.
Maintain a stable uncrossed configuration and monitor. The doll remains outside the basket beyond safe direct reach.
Keep both arms stable and uncrossed with grippers open while monitoring the out-of-reach target; placement remains incomplete.
Maintain stable open-gripper poses and monitor the conveyor. The target remains outside the basket and beyond safe reach.
Hold stable uncrossed poses with open grippers. Monitor the target outside the basket; no safe recovery is currently visible.
Maintain stable open-gripper poses and monitor; the doll remains outside the basket beyond safe reach.
